bullets.title: June NFP misses badly at +57k; Fed on hold through 2026
bullets.body: June nonfarm payrolls came in at 57k (vs. 100–115k consensus), with prior months revised down 74k cumulatively. The unemployment rate fell to 4.2% but entirely due to a 720k drop in labor force participation (not job creation). Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and Wolfe Research all conclude the Fed stays on hold through year-end; September hike odds fell from ~73% to ~17-25% post-print. Fed Chair Warsh at ECB Sintra acknowledged inflation risks have declined, reinforcing the hold narrative.

bullets.title: META's 'Meta Compute' cloud launch sparks AI capex debate and massive unwind
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported META is building a cloud infrastructure business to sell excess AI compute capacity. META stock closed +8.8% on improved ROIC optics, but the move triggered a debate: bears (Ed Zitron, some sell-side) argued it signals overbuild relative to demand, while bulls (Jefferies, MS, KeyBanc, Citi) viewed it as monetization optionality that improves FCF and justifies higher capex. Neocloud names CRWV (-13%) and NBIS (-15%) sold off sharply as META represents >33% and >50% of their backlogs, respectively. MS estimates every 250 MW leased at $40/watt adds ~$3 (8%) to 2028 EPS.

bullets.title: Semi/memory momentum unwind: SOX -9% from June peak; Global Memory -15% in a week
bullets.body: AI infrastructure crowding unwound sharply, with the MS Tech Momentum factor down ~20% MTD—worst month since early 2000s. Semis saw the largest active net reduction, with hedge funds selling Info Tech at -2.7 SDs (4th consecutive week of net selling per GS Prime). MU -13.8% w/w, SNDK -16.5% w/w, COHR -12.4% w/w. The AI Tech Beneficiaries index posted its largest single-day active net reduction on Thursday, July 2. Despite the selloff, UBS maintains DRAM undersupply through 2Q28 and raises 2H26 DDR pricing to +32% QoQ in 3Q from +17% prior; MU PT $1,625.

bullets.title: S&P 500 +1.8% w/w, +9.3% YTD; Q2 earnings expected +22% YoY—broadening narrative intact
bullets.body: Despite the AI/semi unwind, the S&P finished the week up 1.8%; equal-weight RSP hit fresh all-time highs and outpaced cap-weighted by ~70bp. Citi raised its year-end S&P target to 8,100 (on $350/$400 EPS for 2026/2027). FactSet projects Q2 S&P 500 earnings growth of 23.3% YoY—the second consecutive quarter of 20%+ growth. Median S&P 1500 stock is delivering double-digit earnings growth, fastest pace since post-COVID, per multiple strategists. Mag 7 and S&P 493 both expected to deliver 17% EPS growth in 2027, first convergence since 2021.

bullets.title: Hedge funds de-grossing: Tech at -2z; gross leverage at 98th pctile on 5-year; seasonality points to more selling
bullets.body: GS Prime reports US L/S gross leverage rose to 202.9% (2nd pctile 1Y) but hedge funds net sold for 3rd straight week, with Info Tech the most net sold sector at -2.7 SDs. Asia Fundamental L/S sold at the largest monthly rate in records (-2z, second highest monthly selling). JPM Prime Monthly Wrap notes US Momentum down 17% from June 22 peak and flags seasonal de-grossing into late July. Korea and Japan dealers are also short significant gamma via leveraged ETF positioning, amplifying volatility.

bullets.title: AI power/data center buildout intact: AWS EC2 prices +20%, neocloud LTA prices >$10M/MW
bullets.body: Despite the capex debate, demand signals for AI compute remain robust. AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block prices ~20% effective July 1 (second increase this year). LLM token volumes +70% MoM in June, 20x YoY per JPM Data Center Watch; GPU rental prices rose across all tiers. Neocloud long-term contract prices are moving above $10-12M/MW. JPM upgraded AI server TAM forecasts: servers +9/+12/+20% for 2026/27/28; AI servers at +37% CAGR through 2030. ERCOT Batch Zero approved ~35GW baseload demand, supporting IPP contracting opportunity (VST, CEG, GEV).

bullets.title: Memory upcycle thesis reinforced: DRAM spot +10% MoM, +740% YoY; supply deficit extends to 2Q28
bullets.body: PC DDR5 (16Gb) hit $43.14 in spot markets (+10% MoM, +740% YoY). UBS raises 2H26 DRAM contract pricing to +32% QoQ in 3Q26 (from +17%). NAND pricing forecast +30% QoQ in 3Q26. HBM demand raised to 33.1bn Gb in 2026 (+90% YoY). Apple announced 15-25% price hikes across Mac/iPad lines directly attributable to memory cost pressures; Apple is simultaneously lobbying Washington to source memory from sanctioned Chinese suppliers (CXMT, YMTC). Samsung and SK Hynix announced $3.1T combined Korean chip investment through 2040.

bullets.title: Comcast spinning off NBCUniversal/Sky; Charter in SpaceX mobile talks—media/telecom structurally shifting
bullets.body: Comcast announced a tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal and Sky into a separate public company (~1-year timeline); Mike Cavanagh to lead NBCUniversal, Michael Angelakis to lead Cable RemainCo. Wolfe Research upgraded FOXA to Outperform ($71 PT) on ROKU deal, seeing a multi-channel CTV compounder trading at 11.8x NTM UFCF. Charter held exec-level talks with SpaceX on a consumer mobile phone partnership. Verizon announced a 50:50 JV with BT Group for international operations and will record $700-800M loss in Q2. US telecom names (VZ, T) fell 5-10% on Starlink competitive fears.

bullets.title: Macro regime: Fed hawkish tilt, debasement trade roaring back, gold revised down to $4,500/oz 4Q26
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised European growth forecasts while noting the debasement trade (Gold+, Dollar−, steeper curve) is roaring back post-soft NFP. Nine FOMC members now anticipate rate hikes this year, with JPM's base case for first hike in late 2026 or 1Q27 if core PCE stays above 0.21% MoM. Gold price targets revised sharply lower: $4,500 4Q26 (from $6,000) and $5,000 4Q27 (from $6,300) as Iran war premium is removed. Wolfe Research forecasts June core CPI at 0.23% (vs. 0.3% consensus), with headline CPI -0.06% on lower energy—supporting a Fed summer hold.

bullets.title: Iran ceasefire / Hormuz reopening: oil -20% from April peak, reshaping global macro
bullets.body: The Iran-US MoU signed June 17 extended a 60-day ceasefire and reopened the Strait of Hormuz, removing acute energy supply tail risk. Brent crude has fallen from $120/bbl in April to ~$70/bbl, cutting Eurozone inflation from 3.2% to 2.8% in June. JPM cut its 2H26 Brent assumption to $75/bbl (from $85 3Q, $80 4Q). The oil shock removal is a net positive for growth (consumer real income) but creates earnings headwinds for energy sector. Saudi crude shipments recovered to 6.3 mmbbl/d. US gasoline prices remain 28% above pre-conflict levels despite crude normalization.

bullets.title: Rotation into Financials, Healthcare, Consumer—away from AI/semis—gaining institutional momentum
bullets.body: GS and JPM both note capital rotating from AI/Tech into Financials, Healthcare, Consumer, and Software rather than leaving markets. Regional banks (KRE) up 15% since March 31, outperforming SPX by 600bps YTD; 22V favors USB and FITB on loan growth and NIM. Healthcare expected to outperform in 3Q on midterm seasonality (+7.5% historical SPX outperformance) and hedge fund positioning at -2z that is now reversing. Consumer Staples outperformed broader market +3% in June. JPM Healthcare tactical call: add as low-correlation long vs. Tech.

bullets.title: TSLA Q2 deliveries +25% YoY at 480K beat; ENPH surges on potential US ban on Chinese inverters
bullets.body: Tesla Q2 deliveries came in at 480K units, up 25% YoY and beating consensus of ~406K, highest growth rate since 3Q23. Energy storage was 13.5 GWh (+34% YoY). Separately, ENPH surged 11%+ pre-market Monday on Reuters reports that the Trump administration is drafting a ban on foreign (Chinese) solar inverter imports on national security grounds. GEV and NXT would also benefit. Chinese inverters hold ~50% of US utility-scale/C&I market share.

bullets.title: Bloom Energy expands Brookfield AI partnership 5x to $25B; on-site power thesis accelerates
bullets.body: Bloom Energy and Brookfield Infrastructure expanded their AI infrastructure partnership from $5B to $25B (5 GW capacity framework). Brookfield has already committed $1.6B across 6-7 projects totaling 330 MW. MS upgraded BE to Overweight with $310 PT on the news. The expansion underscores structural demand for on-site power as grid interconnection queues lengthen; UBS raised BE PT to $355. Morgan Stanley also initiated Innio (INIO) at Overweight ($47 PT) as a competing reciprocating engine play with 24% revenue CAGR through 2030.

bullets.title: US equity positioning: retail at 89th pctile buying; HFs net sellers; leveraged ETF systemic risk flagged
bullets.body: Retail net bought $36B in equities last week (89th percentile 1Y), with $22B via single stocks. MU ($897M +3.7z) and SNDK ($705M +4.6z) topped retail purchases despite the selloff. JPM flags US margin debt at a record $1.4T and levered ETF assets at $220B, with systemic risk from mechanical rebalancing creating -$16B/1% short gamma near historical highs. Futures traders net sold ~$11.3B. Corporate bond inflows hit $5B (largest in some time), while crypto ETFs saw -$1.7B and US equity ETFs -$10.2B outflows.

bullets.title: ERCOT Batch Zero / data center power in Texas: 35 GW baseload demand, PUCT confirmation mid-August
bullets.body: ERCOT Batch Zero was approved by PUCT two weeks ago with confirmation expected mid-August after finalized load forecast integration. ERCOT has signaled ~35 GW baseload demand and ~65 GW study demand, supporting IPP contracting (NRG secured 5.4 GW H-class turbines from GEV plus EPC agreement with Kiewit). NY legislature is also considering a 1-year pause on large data center permits (Responsible Data Center Development Act). Morgan Stanley notes AI power demand to drive 2.6% annual US electricity demand growth.

bullets.title: USMCA moved to annual reviews; Mexico trade advantage intact near-term, broader uncertainty ahead
bullets.body: The US formally declined to renew USMCA at the July 1 deadline, shifting to annual review through 2036. No immediate tariff changes; treaty remains in force. JPM and others note Mexico retains significant nearshoring advantage, particularly in pharma, semis, and advanced manufacturing. A third round of US-Mexico negotiations is scheduled for mid-July; JPM projects renegotiation could drag into late 2027. Mexico 2Q26 GDP was revised up to 5.5% saar (from 3.3%) on strong April data.

bullets.title: Eurozone recovery confirmed; JPM raises 4Q26–1Q27 GDP; ECB likely to hike once in September
bullets.body: Euro area June composite PMI revised up to 50.0 (+1.4 pts from May), consistent with ~0.8% annualized growth. JPM raised 4Q26–1Q27 GDP to 1.5% (from 1.3%); ECB expected to deliver one final 25bp hike in September as core inflation stays ~2.5% through early 2027 before declining. German government announced 33 reform proposals (€10B tax cuts, labor market flexibility, bureaucracy reduction) that could lift trend growth 20-30bp. Eurozone June headline inflation fell to 2.8% YoY (from 3.2%), driven by energy.

bullets.title: DLR acquires Blackstone's NOVA data center stake for $7.8B; accretive 2027-2028
bullets.body: Digital Realty announced the acquisition of Blackstone's interest in three fully leased Northern Virginia hyperscale data centers (288 MW) for $7.8B gross ($3.5B cash/stock to Blackstone), at a >6.5% initial cap rate with 3.6% annual escalators. The deal is expected to be accretive to Core FFO/share: ~80bps in 2027 and ~330bps in 2028. Citi maintains Buy on DLR with a $226 PT. The transaction signals healthy pricing for stabilized hyperscale assets and removes the 2027 growth gap concern.

bullets.title: Amazon Leo satellite commercialization imminent; SpaceX Starlink competitive fears hit telcos
bullets.body: Amazon launched 29 satellites via Atlas V on July 2, deploying enough total satellites (396) to begin Leo broadband service later in 2026—directly competing with Starlink. Wolfe Research projects Leo at $30B revenue and 63% operating margins by 2035. Charter held exec-level talks with SpaceX on consumer mobile; DT CEO is reportedly pursuing a DT/TMUS merger structure partly driven by Starlink mobile competitive threat. US telecom names (VZ, T) fell 5-10% on LEO competitive concerns.
